main_topics.reason: The user described a three-week flare with thick scaling and itching in several scalp areas despite using medicated shampoos.
The user asked what treatment could follow the shampoos and ended by accepting a plan to ask about topical treatments and soften the scale.
The user asked whether to see a GP or dermatologist and raised long waits for dermatology appointments.
The user specifically asked whether scalp steroids are safe because of concerns about skin thinning and said the answer was reassuring.
The user asked for help with itch that was especially disruptive at night and discussed the difficulty of not scratching.
The user said they were at the end of their rope and later expressed that managing the flare felt like a lot.
The user said visible flakes falling on their shoulders were embarrassing at work.

output.summary: The user described a persistent, itchy scalp psoriasis flare with thick scale that was not responding to tar and ketoconazole shampoos, and said the visible flakes were embarrassing at work. The assistant discussed scale-softening and prescription treatment options, answered questions about steroid safety and access to calcipotriol, and suggested seeing a GP; the user accepted a plan to book an appointment, ask about treatments, use oil on the thick patch, and avoid scratching.
